samples.question: The upper row of five squares is the starting board. Exactly one board square is drawn inside a heavy black frame; that framed square is the one the question is about. Below the board is a row of white cards, and each card holds two coloured swatches with a small arrow pointing from the left swatch to the right one. Each card is a recolouring rule: every board square whose colour is the card's left colour becomes the card's right colour, and every other board square is left exactly as it is. The cards act on the board one at a time, in the order they are drawn from left to right, as the long arrow under the card row shows. A rule that matches nothing when its turn comes changes nothing, and a square that a rule has already recoloured can be recoloured again by a later rule. Every colour in the picture is one of red, amber, green or blue. The board after the cards have acted is not drawn anywhere in the picture. What colour is the framed square after every card has acted? Answer with one word: red, amber, green or blue.
